families.why: The largest measured one-worker gap: #1033 found Zeebra about 31-32x slower than grobx at n = 18 and 20. Dense quadratic systems are the canonical MQ workload. Construction overlaps M34's zb/planted-dense, now in G's confirmation (decision 2026-11-25).

Sampled sparse MQ (4n terms per equation): the sparse-matrix regime, where index and coefficient traffic rather than dense arithmetic should dominate (D). Construction overlaps zb/planted-sparse (G's confirmation).
Genuinely application-derived (radiative transfer, Chandrasekhar 1950; M34 #1006). The only public development family with rows in the 1-300 s band; vdim 2^n, so it also exercises FGLM-scale bases.
families.note: gen-chandrasekhar-h-13 completes on the adaptive (signature) route at Z0 although shipping F4 stops on it, so it is a target, not a frontier.

families.why: Mixed-degree (cubic plus linear terms) structured systems from neural-network models. The mixed-degree M34 public rows (Runge-Kutta) are all under 0.1 s, and zb/planted-dense's mixed rows are sealed.
families.note: noon-8 (<1 s at Z0) is dropped from the target band. noon-10 is a default-limit frontier: adaptive's signature attempt falls back on TooManyRows and shipping F4 then stops on TooManyColumns, while the forced signature engine completes it (dev probe).

families.why: GF(2) MQ: plan section 4.5 needs whole-pipeline attribution for GF(2), where grobx selects its gf2 kernel.

families.note: #1200 (Amendment 1): eco-13 moves from frontier to rows. It is an R2 regime row, and it completes under default limits at Z0 on both fields (f4 110-170 s, adaptive 14-19 s in #1162's probe); it was listed as a frontier for f4's time, not for a refusal.
